name: Coral reef beauty: restored vs healthy vs degraded (pairwise)
description:
Faithful replication of the online survey in Alisa, Razak, Mouquet, Graham, Hemingson, Mouillot, Mars Coral Restoration Project monitoring team, Subhan, Zamani, Vida & Lamont (2025), "Benthic communities on restored coral reefs confer equivalent aesthetic value to healthy reefs", Scientific Reports 15:20790 (3,348 responses from 107 countries). Participants see 30 random pairs of top-down photographs of 50 × 50 cm reef quadrats and click the most beautiful picture, then answer seven background questions (gender, age, country, education, diving or snorkelling, reef knowledge, colour-vision problems). The pool is the paper's 300 survey photographs: 100 natural healthy, 100 restored (Reef Star frames) and 100 degraded rubble quadrats at Pulau Bontosua, Spermonde Archipelago, Indonesia; the habitat is in each file name (H_, R_, D_). The paper turned the choices into Elo scores per photograph and found restored reefs as beautiful as healthy reefs and more beautiful than degraded ones, driven by colour diversity and live coral cover. Photographs from the authors' open repository github.com/alisagita/Aesthetic-value-of-restored-reefs (MIT licence), used with credit; the template is removed if the authors object.

Differences from the original study: (1) photographs are resized from 700 to 560 px to fit the upload limit; (2) the 60 photographs a participant sees are all different (the original drew random pairs and did not say whether a photo could repeat); (3) a consent tick box opens the survey; (4) country is a free-text field instead of a drop-down list; (5) the original ran on biodiful.org in English and French; this template is English only.
author: Alisa, Razak, Mouquet, Graham, Hemingson, Mouillot et al.

elements.title: I agree to take part in this survey and to the anonymous use of my answers for research.

elements.name: beauty_choice
elements.title: Click on the most beautiful picture.
elements.description: 30 pairs per participant. The 60 photographs are drawn at random (no repeats within a participant) from the 300 survey photographs in media folder benthic: 100 natural healthy (H_), 100 restored (R_) and 100 degraded (D_) reef quadrats; the file name gives habitat_site_photo id as in the authors' repository. Value per trial: {chosen, not_chosen, chosen_side left|right, chosen_habitat, other_habitat, position}; shown = [left, right]. Analysis in the paper: Elo score per photograph from all pairwise matches (mean over random match orders), then habitat comparison (mixed model, equivalence test) and image features (colour diversity, live coral cover).
